themes_detail.label: Dead animals surge
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope/Carroll Gardens experienced 8 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK alone—a 611% spike from the 1.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling a potential public health and sanitation crisis that demands immediate investigation into root causes.
evidence: 8 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (611% increase, z-score 6.53)
Spike is contemporaneous with rodent complaints up 229% (14 complaints 2 weeks ago) and illegal dumping up 209%
Convergence suggests environmental degradation or rodent infestation triggering cascading public health complaints
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Department of Sanitation about response protocol and whether they've noticed uptick in Carroll Gardens/Park Slope
Investigate potential link between illegal dumping surge and dead animal complaints—are disposal sites attracting rodents?
Canvass residents on specific blocks with complaints to document hygiene conditions and health concerns

themes_detail.label: Bike rack complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope/Carroll Gardens saw 6 bike rack complaints THIS WEEK—a 1500% spike from the 0.4 weekly average—an unusual pattern that may signal either new infrastructure issues or organized resident pushback on bike parking.
evidence: 6 bike rack complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score 8.08)
Rapid spike suggests either sudden infrastructure failure, new bike lane/rack installation issues, or coordinated resident complaints
No recent Reddit discussions or news coverage identified, making this an underreported emerging issue
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint details to identify which specific streets/locations—pattern may reveal installation defect or conflict
Contact NYC DOT about any recent bike infrastructure installations or maintenance in Carroll Gardens/Park Slope
Interview cycling advocates and residents to understand whether complaints reflect quality-of-life frustration or legitimate safety issues

themes_detail.label: Street condition deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens jumped to 41 THIS WEEK—a 114% spike from the 19.1 weekly average—concurrent with snow/ice season and suggesting infrastructure maintenance gaps that compound winter damage.
evidence: 41 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 19.1 weekly baseline (114% increase, z-score 4.91)
Snow/Ice complaints already at 1210 over 90 days, indicating seasonal pressure on infrastructure
Community Board has repeatedly requested street/water main inspections and repairs—chronic unfunded issue resurging
reporting_angles: Obtain specific street segments from 311 data and map to identify whether complaints cluster in areas with known pothole/structural issues
Interview NYC DOT about response times and resource allocation for this winter season in Community District 306
Cross-reference with CB budget requests: have street inspection/repair requests been funded or remained pending for multiple years?

themes_detail.label: Tree health crisis emerging
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK—a 2300% increase from the 0.1 weekly average—suggesting widespread tree disease, pest damage, or infrastructure stress in the district's parks and streetscapes.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score 8.69)
Damaged tree complaints at 307 over 90 days suggest broader tree stress in district
Community Board budget priorities include park reconstruction/upgrades—tree health may be underlying driver
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks arborist about tree health survey results for Park Slope/Carroll Gardens and whether disease or pests identified
Investigate whether recent weather (late snow/ice documented in 311 data) damaged tree canopy or root systems
Scout specific trees flagged in complaints and photograph condition; interview residents about visible decline

themes_detail.label: Illegal dumping spike continues
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints reached 27 two weeks ago—a 209% spike from the 8.8 weekly average—persisting as a neighborhood environmental and quality-of-life concern that suggests enforcement gaps.
evidence: 27 illegal dumping complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 8.8 weekly baseline (209% increase, z-score 7.19)
Converges with dead animal and rodent spikes, suggesting dumping sites attracting pests and creating public health hazard
Timing suggests sustained issue over past 2 weeks; no recent news coverage or community board discussion identified
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints to identify hotspots for dumping—likely specific blocks or alleyways near parks/vacant lots
Interview NYPD Sanitation Enforcement or NYC Department of Sanitation about patrol frequency and citation rates in district
Document dumping sites with photography; interview nearby residents about frequency and whether enforcement visible
